_comments: The Contracts write API, declared as metadata. CodeGen reads these rows and emits one typed
BaseRemotableOperation subclass per row into the browser-safe Entities package, so the client
imports the CONTRACT without pulling in the server engine.
WHY THESE ARE OPERATIONS AND NOT ACTIONS. The app's master plan (§10.5) originally specified MJ
Actions for status transitions. Orders settled the split for the family the other way — Actions
are for agent/workflow-invocable work, while the operations that MUTATE are the API the UI
calls — and consistency across the bizapps is worth more than this app's original plan text.
Flagged for Amith on PR #2 rather than changed silently.
Every row is GenerationType=Manual: CodeGen emits a typed SHELL and the hand-authored server
subclass in packages/CoreEntitiesServer supplies InternalExecute and registers under the key.
The server subclass registers LAST (it extends the generated base), so it wins ClassFactory
dispatch. AI generation is deliberately not used — these bodies decide what bills and what
stops billing, which is exactly where being subtly wrong produces a plausible wrong invoice.
RequiredScope is 'contracts:write' on all three because all three write. Reads of contract data
go through RunView and the entity layer, which have their own permissions — there is no
read-only operation here to grant separately.

fields.Name: Activate Term
fields.Description: Bring a contract term to life: move it to Active and create the billing schedule plus the billing events its cadence implies, in one transaction. Activation is not a status flip — a term marked Active with no schedule bills nothing, and nobody notices until a quarter closes light. Refuses a term that covers nothing, and refuses to activate twice.

fields.Name: Renew Term
fields.Description: Carry an agreement into its next period: create the successor term pointed back at its predecessor, carry the coverage forward with prices escalated by the agreed percentage, and close the prior term as Completed rather than deleting it. The requested escalation is CLAMPED to the term's negotiated ceiling rather than rejected. PreviewOnly runs the identical computation and writes nothing, so a human can approve the actual numbers before they exist.

fields.Name: Terminate Contract
fields.Description: End an agreement and STOP IT BILLING. Moves the contract and every live term to Terminated, and cancels the scheduled billing events dated after the effective date while leaving the ones on or before it standing — periods already covered are still owed. Events already Generated or Invoiced are never touched: un-billing money that has left the building is an accounting act, not a contract one. PreviewOnly reports the exact cancelled/retained split without writing.

_comments: The one operation here that is NOT a lifecycle transition. SaveContract exists because a BROWSER
cannot compose a contract with its terms and coverage: the client holds the GENERATED entity, and
the child collections live on the server subclass. So the client builds a ContractDraft, and this
rehydrates it into the real tree and delegates to ONE ContractEntityServer.Save().
It decides NOTHING. Every rule — escalation ceilings, term numbering, legal status moves, whether
coverage fits inside its term — stays in the entity subclasses, on the one path every write takes.
A rule added here would be invisible to fixtures, agents and other operations.
A server-side caller does NOT need this: another app constructs ContractEntityServer and calls
Save() directly, which is simpler and typed. Remotable operations are for exposing server work to
the front end, and that is the whole reason this row exists.

fields.Name: Save Contract
fields.Description: Create or update a whole agreement from one payload — contract, terms, coverage, billing schedules and commitments — in a single transaction. A failure anywhere rolls back everything, including the allocated contract number, so a half-written agreement cannot exist. Removals are named explicitly rather than inferred from absence, because a client that loaded a contract lazily holds only some of its terms. Returns the saved agreement re-read from the database, so the caller sees the values the server derived rather than its own guesses.

_comments: Co-terming (master plan §5.4) — the capability standalone subscriptions structurally cannot
provide, and the reason the contract owns the calendar. Adding a product mid-term creates an
amendment plus a line whose EndDate is the TERM's, so the new product renews with everything
else instead of acquiring its own clock.
It applies AddProduct and Coterm only. ContractAmendment records THAT a term changed and of what
kind, not WHICH line changed or to what value, so ChangeQuantity/ChangePrice/PartialTerminate
would have to be guessed — and a wrong guess produces an amendment marked Applied against a term
nothing actually changed on. Refused with the reason instead; raised as Q2 for Andrew.

fields.Name: Amend Term
fields.Description: Change a term that is RUNNING, without restarting it. Adding a product mid-term creates a ContractAmendment plus a co-term line whose window runs from the amendment date to the TERM's end date, so the new product lands on the same renewal date as everything else the customer already has and the stub period prorates on the next billing event. All-or-none: the amendment and the line are written together or neither is. PreviewOnly computes the stub window and its day count without writing. Refuses a term that is not Active, an amendment dated outside its term, and the amendment kinds whose change cannot be derived from the record.
